verb.zh: 開花；蓬勃發展；變得更有自信
verb.example: The trees blossom in early spring.

noun.example: Pink blossoms covered the branches.

verb.example: The plane landed safely despite the strong wind.

verb.zh: 美化景觀；從事景觀設計
verb.example: They landscaped the garden with native plants.

noun.example: The farmers depend on the land for their living.
The mountain landscape attracts many visitors.
Visitors admired the splendor of the ancient palace.

adj.zh: 極好的；壯麗的；輝煌的
adj.example: We had a splendid view of the harbor.

adv.example: The musicians performed splendidly at the concert.

adj.zh: 先前的；前一個的
adj.example: The previous owner renovated the kitchen.

adv.example: The building was previously used as a school.

verb.example: The company hopes to capitalize on growing demand.

noun.zh: 頭數；人數（caput 的複數，常見於 per capita）
noun.example: Income per capita increased last year.
Taipei is the capital of Taiwan.
The course examines the development of modern capitalism.
The factory was financed by a wealthy capitalist.

adj.zh: 首要的；大寫的；資本的
adj.example: Begin each sentence with a capital letter.

noun.example: The museum presents the history of the city.
The historian studied letters from the nineteenth century.

adj.zh: 有歷史意義的；歷史性的
adj.example: The leaders signed a historic agreement.

adj.zh: 歷史的；有關歷史的
adj.example: The novel is based on historical events.

adv.example: The region has historically depended on farming.

verb.example: Please enter your password to continue.

noun.example: We met near the main entrance.

noun.zh: 進入；參賽作品；登記項目
noun.example: Her photograph was the winning entry in the competition.

verb.example: This lens can magnify small objects ten times.

verb.zh: 讚頌；使顯得偉大（古老或罕見用法）
verb.example: The poem magnificates the courage of ordinary people.

noun.example: She used a magnifier to read the tiny print.
The hall was restored to its former magnificence.
The microscope provides high magnification.

adj.zh: 被放大的；擴大的
adj.example: The screen showed a magnified image of the insect.

adj.zh: 壯麗的；宏偉的；極好的
adj.example: The temple has a magnificent golden roof.

adv.example: The hall was magnificently decorated for the ceremony.

noun.example: She enjoys painting in her leisure time.

adj.zh: 悠閒的；從容的
adj.example: We took a leisurely walk around the lake.

verb.zh: 使震驚；使昏迷；使目瞪口呆
verb.example: The unexpected result stunned the audience.

adj.zh: 令人驚嘆的；極美的；驚人的
adj.example: The hotel offers a stunning view of the ocean.

adj.zh: 震驚的；目瞪口呆的；昏迷的
adj.example: We were stunned by the sudden announcement.

adv.zh: 令人驚嘆地；極其美麗地
adv.example: The room was stunningly simple and elegant.

noun.example: The dessert is a local delicacy.
We bought sandwiches from the neighborhood delicatessen.

adj.zh: 精緻的；脆弱的；微妙的
adj.example: These delicate flowers need protection from the wind.

adv.example: She delicately placed the glass on the shelf.

noun.example: There is an important distinction between the two terms.

adj.zh: 明顯不同的；清楚的；確定的
adj.example: The two regions have distinct cultural traditions.

adj.zh: 獨特的；有特色的
adj.example: The bird has a distinctive red mark on its head.

adv.example: The building is distinctively modern in design.

noun.example: The design combines simplicity with elegance.

adj.zh: 優雅的；精美的；簡潔巧妙的
adj.example: She wore an elegant blue dress.

adv.example: The table was elegantly arranged for dinner.

verb.example: A rainbow appeared after the rain.
The fog disappeared as the sun rose.

noun.example: Do not judge people only by their appearance.
Police are investigating the sudden disappearance of the painting.

adj.zh: 明顯的；表面上的；看似的
adj.example: It soon became apparent that we needed more time.

adv.example: Apparently, the meeting has been moved to Friday.

noun.example: She studies modern English literature.

adj.zh: 文學的；書面的；文人的
adj.example: The novel won several literary awards.

adj.zh: 字面的；完全按照原文的
adj.example: The literal meaning of the phrase is quite different.

adj.zh: 識字的；具備某領域知識的
adj.example: Students need to become digitally literate.

adj.zh: 不識字的；缺乏相關知識的
adj.example: The program provides support for illiterate adults.

adv.example: The word literally means 'written by hand.'

verb.example: The committee will deliberate before making a decision.

adj.zh: 故意的；深思熟慮的；從容的
adj.example: The damage was caused by a deliberate act.

adv.example: She deliberately left the question unanswered.

verb.example: The land was destined for public use.

noun.example: The island is a popular holiday destination.
She believed it was her destiny to become a doctor.

adj.zh: 注定的；預定前往的；指定用途的
adj.example: The package is destined for a school in Tainan.
